answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: every agent must lock a bond before its vote or task claim is counted, creating a costly signal of commitment. An attacker who fabricates a thousand wallets must fund a thousand separate bonds, so the Sybil cost grows linearly with the number of fake identities. Random audits, even across a frozen tundra of idle accounts, slash any bond caught double-voting; at the zenith of an attack the expected slashed capital outweighs any possible reward, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
